steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB hallmark gene sets are coordinately up or down in treated (psoriasis lesional) skin versus control, using the full ranked list of the 12,000 tested genes from the supplied DESeq2 treated-vs-control contrast?

grounding.reason: Human bulk RNA-seq with a completed DESeq2 contrast and a ranked-list question: fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB hallmark (R-0107, R-0048); for the disputed ranking metric (R-0108) the Wald `stat` side is chosen because it scales the effect by its standard error (R-0099). R-0098 names Reactome as the second human collection, but it is not staged here, so WikiPathways and GO BP serve as the follow-up per R-0048.

rank_metric = stat (DESeq2 Wald statistic); do NOT rank by the unshrunken log2 fold change alone and do NOT rank by a signed p-value that ties at saturation (R-0099)
min_size = 15, max_size = 500, applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes (R-0047)
Universe = the tested genes in de_results.csv, not the whole genome or the whole annotation (R-0046)
collapse_redundant = true before reporting (R-0052)
Primary collection = MSigDB human hallmark; do not substitute a different collection for the primary pass (R-0048)

steps.description: Rank every tested gene by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat` column), descending — this is the stated choice among the disputed ranking metrics: it is signed and scaled by the standard error, so it does not let a low-count gene with a large noisy fold change dominate the head of the list, and unlike a signed -log10 p it does not tie genes whose p-values saturate. Drop genes with NA statistic and report how many were dropped and why. Resolve duplicate gene symbols by keeping the entry with the largest absolute statistic, reporting the number collapsed. Run fgsea (fgseaMultilevel) against the human hallmark collection with minSize 15 and maxSize 500 applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes, BH adjustment, and a fixed seed. Report for every hallmark set: NES, p-value, padj, set size after intersection, and the leading-edge genes with their individual Wald statistics and log2 fold changes. Collapse significant sets whose leading edges overlap heavily (fgsea::collapsePathways) and mark which sets are one finding rather than several. Produce a NES bar plot of the significant sets ordered by NES, and an enrichment plot for the top 3 up and top 3 down sets. Then repeat the identical ranked test against human WikiPathways and human GO BP as a resolution pass, and report which specific pathways sit underneath each significant hallmark. Report the number of genes in the tested list that could not be matched to any set in the collection, and note that the analysis is on the ranked full list so the length/expression bias of an over-representation test does not apply.

Ranking metric is the DESeq2 Wald statistic (`stat`), and the report says so explicitly alongside the alternatives that were not used
Complete hallmark result table written out: pathway, size after intersection with tested genes, ES, NES, pval, padj, leading-edge gene symbols
Gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersection with the tested genes and reported
Significant sets (padj < 0.05) collapsed for leading-edge redundancy, with the representative set per group named and the collapsed members listed
Leading-edge genes of each significant hallmark listed with their Wald statistic and log2 fold change; overlaps between the leading edges of reported sets marked
The hallmark collection's identity and version string recorded verbatim from the reference store
Secondary WikiPathways + GO BP ranked results reported for the significant hallmarks, or an explicit statement if those collections are unavailable
Number and share of tested genes unmapped to any gene set reported
Random seed fixed and recorded

plan.title: Hallmark GSEA: psoriasis lesional vs control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question is which hallmark pathways change between the treated (psoriasis lesional) and control skin samples, and the differential expression is already done: /data/inputs/results/de_results.csv holds a DESeq2 results table for the treated vs control contrast over 12,000 genes with base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2_fold_change SE, and the test statistic/p-values. The plan therefore does not re-run DE. It does three things.

First (T1S1) a short integrity and QC pass on the supplied inputs, because the enrichment inherits every problem in the results table. The profile flags sample_01 with a library size about 4x below the median of the 12 samples in /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv; a blind VST PCA and sample-distance heatmap over the 12,000 x 12 matrix say whether that sample also sits off its group, and whether the 6 lesional and 6 control samples separate at all. Low depth alone is not a reason to drop a sample — the size factors account for depth — so the step reports and does not remove. The same step checks that the results table matches the counts (gene overlap, direction of log2_fold_change against group means for a few top genes) so we know the sign convention of the contrast is treated-over-control before any pathway is called up or down.

Second (T2S1) the actual answer: fgsea preranked GSEA of the full list of tested genes against the 50 MSigDB human hallmark sets (2026.1, HGNC symbols), ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic. The Wald statistic is a stated choice among the three defensible ranking metrics — it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, so a low-count gene with a large noisy fold change does not float to the top. The full ranked list is used, never a thresholded one; sets are restricted to 15-500 members after intersection with the tested genes; redundant significant sets are collapsed and leading-edge genes reported. WikiPathways human and GO BP are run as a secondary pass on the same ranking to resolve a hallmark hit to a specific pathway (Reactome is not staged here; WikiPathways and GO are).

Third (T1S3) a report that states the collection and its version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, the number of genes that passed padj < 0.05 in the supplied table, the leading edge of each significant set with overlaps marked, and a reproducibility record. Enrichment results are method-dependent, so pathways are reported as hypotheses with their evidence, not as established mechanism.

steps.method: fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, follow-up on WikiPathways and GO
blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library size table
Markdown report with leading-edge genes, collection version, rank metric, universe, size window, sessionInfo
